channel.title: Facts Should Know
channel.description: Short, sourced explainers on surprising facts from Facts Should Know.

item.title: The Cutty Sark was reportedly clocked at about 17 knots under sail
item.description: Cutty Sark, launched in 1869, was reportedly capable of about 17 knots under sail. Here is what that figure means, and what it does not.

item.title: Wombats are the only animals that produce cube-shaped poop
item.description: Wombats leave 80 to 100 cubic pellets a day to mark territory. The shape comes from regions of varying stiffness in the final part of the intestine.

item.title: Mantis shrimp can see 12 primary colors while humans see only 3
item.description: Mantis shrimp have 12 to 16 photoreceptor types to our three, yet they tell similar colors apart less precisely than humans do. Here is why.

item.title: Whales evolved from land mammals; Pakicetus walked on four legs about 50 million years ago
item.description: Pakicetus, a land-dwelling cetacean from Pakistan about 50 million years old, has a whale-type ear feature and helps show whales came from land mammals.

item.title: The Eiffel Tower grows 6 inches taller in summer heat
item.description: The Eiffel Tower's iron expands in hot weather and can add up to about 15 cm in height. Here is where the figure comes from and what limits it.

item.title: Ada Lovelace published an algorithm for Babbage's Analytical Engine in 1843
item.description: Ada Lovelace's 1843 notes on Babbage's Analytical Engine included a method for Bernoulli numbers. Why it is called the first program, and why that is…

item.title: Booksellers took up Darwin's 1,250-copy first printing of Origin of Species in 1859
item.description: Darwin's first printing of 1,250 copies was reportedly taken up by booksellers before 24 November 1859. Here is what that does and does not mean.

item.title: Saturn's main rings span about 282,000 km but are typically only about 10 meters thick
item.description: Saturn's main rings span about 282,000 km yet are typically only about 10 meters thick. Here is what they are made of and where the numbers vary.

item.title: Butterflies taste with their feet to identify plants for laying eggs
item.description: Female butterflies drum leaves with taste receptors on their feet, a final chemical check before laying eggs on a suitable host plant.

item.title: Octopuses have nine brains and three hearts but still live only 5 years
item.description: Octopuses have nine brains and three hearts but live only 1-5 years, programmed by evolution to die shortly after reproducing.
